chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Maskin, from al-Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Basir, who said:

I said to him, 'I hear the sneeze, so I praise God and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while I am in prayer.' He said, 'Yes, even if there is a sea between you and your companion.'

key_terms.الْيَمُّ: the sea (used here to denote great distance)
key_terms.وَأُصَلِّي عَلَى النَّبِيِّ: and sending blessings upon the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Can I send blessings upon the Prophet and praise God when someone sneezes during my prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of responding to a sneeze with *Hamd* and *Salawat* during prayer, even if the sneezer is distant. The phrase 'even if it is the sea' (*al-yamm*) serves as a hyperbolic emphasis on the breadth of this concession, highlighting the Shia scholarly view that such acts are *mustahabb* (recommended) rather than obligatory, thus preserving the flow of prayer without invalidating it through excessive movement or speech.
